newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut formalizes tobacco, liquor ad ban.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut formalizes tobacco, liquor ad ban.

text.p: Connecticut lawmakers agreed with the state's main outdoor media group on Friday to officially ban tobacco and alcohol advertisements on billboards within 500 feet of schools.

Outdoor Advertising Association of Connecticut Inc (OAAC) also agreed to donate 30 billboards across the state -- including some near schools -- for anti-tobacco and anti-alcohol ads, Senate President Pro Tempore Kevin Sullivan said.

"The Outdoor Advertising Association deserves credit for recognizing the seriousness and importance of the issue, agreeing to formalize the ban on this type of advertising, and for donating the billboard space," Sullivan, a Democrat, said. "There's no need to legislate something you can achieve by agreement."
OAAC, which sells advertising on 99 percent of Connecticut's commercial billboards, already observed a voluntary ban on tobacco and alcohol ads within 500 feet of schools.
The agreement on Friday formalized the arrangement.
Sullivan said that as a result, he would drop billboards from the bill he is sponsoring to ban tobacco and alcohol advertising within 500 feet of schools and on public transportation.
